question: Why is the supreme Lord called Vama in the ordering of difference?
premises: The Lord desires to make things his own.
He brings about the withdrawal of their differences.
This activity occurs within the ordering of difference.
inference: Therefore, in the ordering of difference, the supreme Lord is called Vama because he reabsorbs differences into himself.
plain_english: Desiring to make them his own, he brings about the withdrawal of their differences. Therefore, in the ordering of difference, this supreme Lord is called Vama.
